```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("_common.R")
do_files <- link_or_text(
  vars$code$stata,                                                          # set once the do-files are published
  "Download the do-files",                                                  # the link text from then on
  "The do-files will be published on this page once they are cleaned up"   # what the page says until then
)
```

The paper's regressions and several of its tables and figures are estimated in Stata. `r do_files`. They read a
Stata copy of the contracts table of [the database](data.qmd#part-core) and Compustat data from WRDS, which are
licensed and not published ([what needs WRDS](reproduce.qmd#what-needs-wrds)).

## Reading the tables

The tables of the database are parquet files, and no `.dta` files are published. Stata reads a table once it has been
converted with R or Python; the codebooks give each column's name in Stata (`StataName`).

## Slicing a span

Span offsets count characters from 0, the end exclusive
([span offsets](data.qmd#span-offsets-are-0-based-and-half-open)). Stata's `usubstr()` counts characters where
`substr()` counts bytes, so a span is sliced with `usubstr()`. For the date spans, with each span's document text,
`TextRaw`, merged on `DocID`:

```stata
generate DateSlice = usubstr( ///
  TextRaw,                    /// the document's text, as every offset reads it
  DateStart + 1,              /// Stata counts from 1, the offsets from 0
  DateStop - DateStart        /// a length in characters, not an end
)
```
